title: Re-engagement programme from a subscriber export
prompt:
Sorrel Kitchen is a weekly meal-kit subscription. Email engagement has slipped and the lifecycle manager wants a re-engagement programme for subscribers who have stopped opening. You are supplied the company's email policy and the subscriber export as CSV. Today is 2026-06-01. Every count you cite must come from the export.

Use these definitions exactly:
- Mailable: `consent_status` is subscribed, `hard_bounce` is no and `spam_complaint` is no.
- Lapsed: mailable, and `last_open_date` is earlier than 2026-03-03 or blank.
- Lapsed buyers are lapsed subscribers with an `orders_count` of 1 or more; lapsed non-buyers have 0.
- Long-dormant: lapsed, and `last_open_date` is earlier than 2025-06-01 or blank.

Deliver the programme: who is in the audience and who is left out, with the count and the reason for each exclusion; the segments and what each receives; the emails themselves, each with its send timing, its subject line, the one thing it asks the reader to do, and a short summary of the body; and what happens to people who respond and to people who do not. Follow the email policy.

End the programme with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer, each line starting with the label:

A1: <number of mailable subscribers>
A2: <number of lapsed subscribers>
A3: <number of lapsed buyers>
A4: <number of lapsed non-buyers>
A5: <number of long-dormant subscribers>

This is a plan for review. Send nothing and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all 5 labeled answers A1-A5 are present and parseable.
A1 states the number of mailable subscribers; full credit for the exact count, zero credit ten or more off.
A2 states the number of lapsed subscribers; full credit for the exact count, zero credit eight or more off.
A3 states the number of lapsed buyers; full credit for the exact count, zero credit six or more off.
A4 states the number of lapsed non-buyers; full credit for the exact count, zero credit six or more off.
A5 states the number of long-dormant subscribers; full credit for the exact count, zero credit five or more off.
The main re-engagement flow has exactly three emails, and each has a send timing, a subject line, a single ask and a body summary.

skill_adherence.check: The plan explicitly leaves out all five groups the policy excludes: unsubscribed, never consented (imported), pending confirmation, hard bounces, and spam complaints.
The plan does not propose emailing unsubscribed or never-consented people, including those with past orders, in this programme or as a separate win-back send.

The only incentive is 10% off with code COMEBACK10, valid for 14 days, offered to lapsed buyers only; lapsed non-buyers are offered the 'Five 20-Minute Dinners' recipe pack and no discount. Any other discount, gift or free box fails.

Emails in the flow are at least 5 days apart, and the plan says every email carries an unsubscribe link and a link to email preferences. A subject line that uses 'Re:' or 'Fwd:' or invented urgency fails.
Long-dormant subscribers receive one last-chance email only, not the three-email flow.

Every count and rate presented as a fact is derivable from the subscriber export under the stated definitions. The plan states no open-rate, revenue or win-back forecast as if it were data; any target or benchmark is labelled as an assumption.

best_practices.check: People who open, click or order leave the flow at once, and people who have not opened or clicked 7 days after their final email are suppressed from marketing.
Lapsed buyers and lapsed non-buyers get messages that differ in substance and fit their history, not the same email with only the offer line changed.
The three subject lines say plainly what each email is about and differ from one another in angle, not only in wording.
